summary.intent: Use the GSD manager dashboard to drive milestone v2.0 to completion for cipher-box — verify, plan, and execute remaining phases (69–79), including background-parallelized planning/execution across quota resets, and ship Phase 74 through the full post-execution gate pipeline (verify/secure/validate/simplify/SDK-E2E/CodeRabbit/PR).
summary.outcome: Phases 70.1, 75, and 77 were fully planned, executed, verified, and merged; Phase 69's false 'Executing' status was root-caused and fixed (plan-scanner filename bug). Phase 74 was planned, executed, audited, and opened as PR #607, but its desktop-e2e gate caught a real runtime bug (hex/base64 encoding mismatch in grant re-mint) plus a dirty-resume security gap, both left as an in-progress gap-closure fix. Phase 76 was stopped by the user before starting; 78/79 remain unplanned. A cross-cutting hex/base64 wire-encoding hardening phase was scoped and filed as a todo per explicit user request.

repo: cipher-box's plan-file scanner has a loose fallback that counts any .md file merely containing the substring 'PLAN' (case-insensitive) as a plan file, causing false phase-status regressions (e.g. '69-WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md' miscounted due to 'PLANE').
Manager dashboard's is_active flag just means 'a file in the phase dir was modified in the last 5 minutes' — not an indicator of a real running agent.

The share API wire contract uses hex encoding uniformly (all 4 share DTOs validate `encryptedReadKey`/`encryptedWriteKey`/`itemNameEncrypted` via `/^(?:[0-9a-fA-F]{2})+$/`), while internal node-codec sealed refs use base64 — same Uint8Array type, opposite required encodings, nothing enforces the right one at a call site, and unit tests mock the API so mismatches only surface in e2e/prod.
vitest does not load .env files — SDK_E2E_SECRET must be exported inline in the shell or the harness silently falls back to a wrong default secret, producing false 401s.
Desktop E2E CI workflow is dispatch-gated, not automatically triggered on PR — must be manually `gh workflow run` dispatched against the branch.

EnterWorktree cannot pin a sub-agent launched at the repo root into a pre-existing worktree ('repo root, not an isolated worktree') — background worktree-isolated planning cannot be resumed via EnterWorktree from a fresh session.
The gsd commit helper sometimes false-negatives `commit_failed` while the commit actually lands — must verify with `git log`, never blindly retry.
Pre-commit hooks in this monorepo (lint-staged) are slow (~1-2 min) — a 'hung' commit is usually just slow, not stuck.

CodeRabbit CLI (local, pre-push) and CodeRabbit's PR-level web review surface different findings — the web review found more code-level issues including a Greptile P1-security flag, on a crypto/durability PR.

code.finding: SentShareResponse doc comments mislabeled base64-encoded fields (encrypted_read_key/encrypted_write_key) as 'Hex-encoded'; item_name_encrypted is correctly hex.

Grant re-mint base64_encode's the wrapped read key for the share-grant wire field, but every share API DTO validates that field as hex — causes a 400 at runtime, only caught by desktop-e2e, not unit tests.

TS rotatedNodes map stores the same Uint8Array reference (aliased with parentNewReadKey) rather than cloning like Rust's engine.rs does — currently safe because nothing zeros parentNewReadKey, but a latent data-loss/zeroization hazard if that changes.
is_active computed purely from 'file modified in last 5 minutes', causing false-positive 'currently executing' dashboard states after any doc edit.
Plan-file matcher has a loose /PLAN/i substring fallback beyond the *-PLAN.md pattern, causing miscounted plan totals when non-plan docs contain 'PLAN' as a substring.

workflow: The ship-phase pipeline sequence is: verify → secure → crypto/privacy review (conditional) → built-in security review → validate (Nyquist) → simplify → SDK-E2E gate → CodeRabbit CLI → conventional-commit reword → ship/PR → resolve PR reviews → extract learnings.

When background worktree-isolated planning agents die mid-run (e.g. from quota limits), the robust recovery is NOT re-entering the worktree via EnterWorktree — instead switch the main checkout to the existing feat branch and run planning/execution inline/sequentially there, since feat branches persist committed work even if the worktree is removed.

CronCreate can schedule autonomous one-shot resumes timed to quota reset windows, letting long multi-phase pipelines survive session limit interruptions if the resume prompt is self-contained and states the corrected recovery method.

Delegating heavy self-contained gate stages (audit gates, SDK-E2E gate, review-thread resolution) to sub-agents lets the orchestrator keep dashboard/branch state clean while conserving the shared runtime stack for one exclusive user at a time.

friction: Session quota limit was hit repeatedly (multiple 'You've hit your session limit' interruptions), killing in-flight background planner agents and forcing multi-stage recovery.

The EnterWorktree-based recovery pattern for resuming stalled background planners was a dead end — required detecting the failure, committing orphaned draft work, removing dead worktrees, and pivoting to a different (sequential main-checkout) strategy.

A stale `node dist/main.js` API process on :3000 (started with a mismatched TEST_LOGIN_SECRET) caused a false 401/all-tests-skipped result that looked like a phase defect but was purely environment drift.
vitest not loading .env caused a second, distinct false failure (empty/default secret) even after the API was correctly restarted from source.

Dashboard falsely displayed Phase 69 as '◆ Executing' due to two compounding bugs (a UAT-artifact requirement gap and a plan-count scanner false positive) — required deep multi-step root-causing before the real fix (renaming one file) was found.
An internal sub-agent's self-made background-wait loop stalled Phase 75's planning agent, requiring a relaunch with explicit 'no self-made background waits' instructions.

The Desktop-E2E Windows leg failed on Phase 74 due to a real hex/base64 encoding bug in grant re-mint — this is described as a recurring class of bug that has bitten the project multiple times before.
CI Typecheck failed after Phase 74 shipped because widened type `RotateReadResult.rotatedNodes` broke a mocked test fixture that vitest didn't type-check at runtime.
User had to interject twice to redirect autonomous work: stopping Phase 76 before it began, and calling out the recurring hex/base64 issue for a durable fix rather than another one-off patch.
open_items: Phase 74 gap-closure fix agent in progress for 3 defects: SC#2 re-mint base64→hex wire encoding, dirty-resume rotatedNodes revocation-bypass gap (medium security, both Rust+TS engines), and a stale-ref desktop-e2e assertion — PR #607 unmerged pending this.

New hardening-phase todo filed: `.planning/todos/pending/2026-07-11-hex-base64-wire-encoding-domain-hardening.md` (severity high) — named boundary codecs, branded types, contract test, and doc reconciliation for the hex-vs-base64 domain split.
Todo: server DTO codegen mislabels (encryptedReadKey/encryptedWriteKey docs say 'hex' but are base64) — requires `pnpm api:generate` + committed client regen, deferred as out-of-phase-scope.
Todo: TS `rotatedNodes` defensive-copy parity fix (match Rust's `.clone()` to remove the aliasing hazard).
Todo: re-mint trusts server for recipient-pubkey binding (MEDIUM security finding), logged rather than fixed inline.
Phases 76, 78, 79 remain unplanned/not started for milestone v2.0 closeout.
Phase 77's live sdk-e2e client→API round-trip was not run for the TEE wire-field rename — flagged as an optional deeper check before merge.
